vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: mails-for-agent
Version: 1.5.1

The 'Mails for Agent' skill provides a standard interface for an AI agent to interact with an email service via a REST API. It includes functionality for sending/receiving emails, searching inboxes, and extracting verification codes or structured data. The skill relies on user-provided environment variables (MAILS_API_URL, MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN) and uses curl for communication. No indicators of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized command execution were found in SKILL.md or _meta.json.

llm.summary: The skill's declared requirements (curl + MAILS_API_URL, MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN, MAILS_MAILBOX) match its email-send/receive purpose, but small inconsistencies in the instructions (an undocumented RESEND_API_KEY and a few timeout/constraint mismatches) and the fact that it will be given a bearer token that can read/send mailbox contents mean you should verify the service and token scope before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (send & receive email via HTTP API) align with the declared requirements: curl and three env vars (MAILS_API_URL, MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN, MAILS_MAILBOX). That set of inputs is proportionate for an HTTP-based mail service.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md is an instruction-only file and confines the agent to calling the provided HTTP endpoints using the three env vars and curl. It does not instruct the agent to read local files or unrelated environment variables. It does show use of curl -o to save attachments (expected). However, some instructions/tables are inconsistent: the API reference examples use MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN for /api/send, while the API Endpoints table says POST /api/send requires a different secret (RESEND_API_KEY). Also timeout values are inconsistent (code long-poll examples allow 60s but Constraints say max 55s). These discrepancies could lead to unexpected behavior or missing required secrets at runtime.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — instruction-only. This is low-risk from install-supply-chain perspective (nothing is downloaded or written to disk by an installer).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests three env vars which are reasonable for an email HTTP API. However the SKILL.md also references a RESEND_API_KEY in the API Endpoints table which is not declared in requires.env. That undocumented secret requirement is a red flag: the skill may need additional credentials not listed, or the docs are out-of-date. Because MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN gives bearer access to read/send/delete mailbox contents, ensure that token's scope is minimal and that MAILS_API_URL points to a trusted provider.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no install-time persistence. The skill is user-invocable and allows autonomous invocation (the platform default) but does not request permanent/always-on privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to be a simple wrapper around an HTTP mail API and mostly behaves as described, but take these precautions before installing:
- Verify MAILS_API_URL is a trusted service endpoint (not a third-party you don't control). The skill will send your bearer token with every request.
- Confirm what MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN can do: prefer a token scoped only to the mailbox and limited to necessary actions (read/send/list/delete if required). Avoid using broad or long-lived credentials.
- Ask the publisher (or inspect provider docs) about the undocumented RESEND_API_KEY referenced in the API table — if that key is required, you should know why and where it is stored.
- Be aware the agent may download attachments to disk using curl -o; avoid pointing it at mailboxes that receive untrusted attachments or limit binary handling.
- Because the skill can read verification codes and delete messages, only grant access to mailboxes created for automation or testing, not your primary personal/business inbox.
- If you intend to allow autonomous agent invocation, restrict which prompts or flows can trigger email actions, and monitor usage and logs for unexpected sends or deletions.
If you can get confirmation from the skill author that RESEND_API_KEY is not required (or that it is documented and justified and will be provided securely), and you limit token scope, this skill is reasonable to use. Otherwise delay installation until the credential discrepancy is resolved.
